Operators can now tune the OAuth access-token lifetime with `EZPDS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECS` (default 900 seconds, accepted range 1–1800). The conformance suite uses it to test what a client sees when its token expires.

Everything's green on main and production is sitting at `v0.10.2`. Here's the picture:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The workspace version is the single source of truth.** `Cargo.toml [workspace.package].version` flows into every crate, gets reported live at `_health/describeServer` via `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, and `just release` *derives* the tag from it. Tag and reported version structurally cannot drift — and a `verify-release` CI job on the `production` branch re-asserts it.
- **Deploys are pull-based, not push-based.** Nothing in CI runs `railway up`; Railway watches the `production` branch with "Wait for CI" on. So "releasing" is really just advancing a git branch pointer — the deploy is Railway noticing.
- **Changelog fragments avoid merge conflicts.** Each PR drops its own file in `changelog.d/`; `set-version` collates them into a dated CHANGELOG section and deletes them. 20 are pending.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

State: `main` = `5b5c74ee`, 22 commits and 20 changelog fragments ahead of `v0.10.2`. CI, iOS TestFlight, and CodeQL all green on the tip.

The one genuine judgment call is the version number, and it's yours to make — the tag is what operators see:

---
name: reference_devenv_shell_invocation
description: How to run one-off build/test commands inside this repo's devenv from a script (insecure-pnpm block + -c-vs--- gotchas)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Running cargo/pnpm here needs the devenv shell (toolchain lives in `.devenv/profile/bin`, not on PATH). Two gotchas bit me (2026-07-21, MM-445 wallet work):

1. **`devenv shell` refuses to enter**, erroring `Refusing to evaluate package 'pnpm-9.15.9' … because it is marked as insecure`. Fix: prefix `NIXPKGS_ALLOW_INSECURE=1` and pass `--impure`.
2. **`devenv shell --impure -c "<cmd>"` silently drops to an interactive prompt** (loads the env via direnv, prints the `(devenv)` prompt, never runs `<cmd>`, exits 0 on EOF — looks like success but did nothing). The `-- <argv>` form DOES execute.

Working recipe (run a script, capture full output):
```
cd /Users/jacob.zweifel/workspace/malpercio-dev/ezpds
NIXPKGS_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 devenv shell --impure -- bash /abs/path/to/script.sh > /abs/out.log 2>&1
```
Run with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` (nix + cargo need it). direnv auto-loads `.env.local` + exports SDKROOT inside. For wallet iOS/host builds the script still needs `export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1; source apps/identity-wallet/scripts/ios-env.sh; export SDKROOT=$(xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path)` — see [[reference_wallet_host_tests_sdkroot]].

Note: this repo's checkout at `/Users/.../ezpds` (the `main` worktree path) is often already ON the feature branch, so edit + build there directly rather than in the sparse nested `.claude/worktrees/<name>` dir — see [[reference_worktree_branch_vs_main_checkout]].

**From a nested worktree (no `.devenv`), borrow the main checkout's built devenv via `nix develop`** (2026-07-22, custos v0.7.2 release prep): `cd /Users/.../ezpds && NIXPKGS_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 nix develop --impure --accept-flake-config --command bash /abs/script.sh`. Use `--command bash <script>` — on nix 2.29 the `-- bash <script>` separator form is rejected ("unexpected argument"), and `-c` fails too. `nix develop` resets cwd to the *worktree* after entering, so `cd` to the worktree path inside the script; `cargo`/`just`/`node` then resolve, and running `just set-version`/`just docs-generate`/`just changelog-check`/`just docs-check` from the worktree operates on the worktree's files. Sandbox off. This ran the whole `just set-version 0.7.2` + docs regen + gate validation for the release PR cleanly.
---
name: reference-worktree-cargo-via-main-devenv
description: "Run cargo in a git worktree without a 20-min cold devenv build — borrow the main checkout's built .devenv and target the worktree manifest"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: b0898d3f-8e24-48e5-a699-d4803d55fbc4
---

In a `.claude/worktrees/*` checkout, `cargo` is **not on PATH** and the worktree has **no `.devenv/`** built — entering its shell (`nix develop`) triggers a cold build (20+ min without the Cachix cache). But the **main checkout** (`/Users/jacob.zweifel/workspace/malpercio-dev/ezpds/.devenv/profile`) is already built, and `rustup` toolchains are user-level (`~/.rustup`, shared).

**So run cargo through the main checkout's devenv, targeting the worktree's manifest:**

```bash
cd /Users/jacob.zweifel/workspace/malpercio-dev/ezpds && \
  nix develop --impure --accept-flake-config -c \
  cargo test --manifest-path <WORKTREE>/Cargo.toml -p <crate>
```

`CARGO_HOME`/registry cache come from the main checkout's `.devenv` (just a cache — fine to share); build artifacts land in the **worktree's** `target/`. First compile of a crate's full dep tree is heavy; reruns are incremental and fast.

Gotchas:
- These commands need broad fs + network (crates.io) access → run with the sandbox **disabled** (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox`). The plain `nix develop` also fails under sandbox with `cannot connect to socket at '/nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket': Operation not permitted` — same fix. Network git (tangled `knot.malpercio.dev` SSH, GitHub mirror) also needs sandbox off — `knot.malpercio.dev` is not in the sandbox allowlist.
- `cd` resets after each Bash call (the shell prints "Shell cwd was reset to <worktree>"), so prefix every invocation with the `cd /main-checkout &&`.
- `nix develop`'s `enterShell` runs `rustup toolchain install` (fast no-op if present) and prints devenv task lines before your command's output — `tail`/`grep` past them.
- **`--manifest-path` is load-bearing, and subagents get this wrong.** The main checkout is often on a *different branch* than the worktree. A subagent that `cd`s to the main checkout and runs a bare `cargo build -p <crate>` (no `--manifest-path`) silently compiles the **main checkout's branch**, not the worktree — producing a green "1294 tests passed" that has nothing to do with the code under review. Seen twice in one session (an implementor and a bug-fixer both reported false green this way while the worktree crate didn't even compile). **Verify build/test/clippy claims first-hand** with `--manifest-path <WORKTREE>/Cargo.toml`; don't trust subagent build evidence in a worktree. To defeat stale-`target/` false negatives, `touch` the changed source files before `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets ... -- -D warnings` so it re-analyzes them.

- **`cargo fmt --all` and `cargo metadata --locked` (lock-check) DO NOT WORK in a nested worktree** (2026-07-08, cost a red CI push). Workspace-`exclude`d packages (the vendored Tauri plugins) make cargo walk *up past the worktree root* to the **main checkout's** `Cargo.toml`, which doesn't exclude the worktree's copy → "current package believes it's in a workspace when it's not". cargo-fmt shells to cargo-metadata internally, so it fails too — printing its **usage/help text and a nonzero exit that a `| grep | head` pipeline masks as success** (pipeline exit = last command; same family as [[reference_sandbox_path_drop_in_pipelines]]'s PIPESTATUS gotcha). Echo `$?` of the *cargo command itself*, never the pipeline. Workarounds: format/check with **bare `rustfmt --edition 2021 [--check] <files…>`** on the files changed in the branch (`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.rs'`); skip local lock-check and let CI's flat checkout run it. Targeted `cargo test/clippy --manifest-path … -p <crate>` are unaffected.

  **2026-07-10 refinements:** (a) **package-scoped fmt works in-worktree** — `cargo fmt -p pds -p common -p crypto -p repo-engine -p identity-wallet -p admin-companion --check` (every workspace member, skipping the vendored plugins) is a cleaner substitute for `fmt --all --check` than bare rustfmt; (b) `just lock-check` (`cargo metadata --locked`) **passed** when run from the worktree root that day — try it before assuming failure; only `fmt --all` reproducibly breaks. A full `just ci-pds` mirror with just the fmt line swapped ran green end-to-end from the worktree.

Related: [[reference_disk_space_worktree_targets]] (each worktree's `target/` is separate, ~GB).

name: release-process-gotchas
description: Practical gotchas when running the documented release flow (set-version → release → deploy-production)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3f781e1f-a2ed-422b-90e0-628aae42bd84
  modified: 2026-07-23T03:19:43.046Z
---

Running the ezpds release flow end-to-end (validated 2026-07-18, v0.7.0; also 2026-07-17, v0.6.0):

- **A version bump breaks `docs-check` unless you also `just docs-generate` in the
  same PR.** The docs-site reference pages (`sites/docs/.../operator/reference/{api,config,ipc}.md`)
  are version-stamped from `Cargo.toml` by `scripts/generate-docs-reference.mjs`;
  `docs-check` (PDS gate) runs it with `--check` and exits 1 when stale. So after
  `just set-version X.Y.Z`, run `just docs-generate` and commit the three regenerated
  pages into the set-version PR, or the PDS gate fails. Diff is stamp-only when no
  route/config/IPC surface changed. (The changelog gate itself is auto-waived on a
  release roll-up: version bump + new `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG section is detected.)
- `just release` refuses a dirty tree, and an **untracked `devenv.lock`** in the
  main checkout counts as dirty — move it aside for the tag/promote commands and
  restore it (open question for the user: commit or gitignore it).
- The dev shell is not active in fresh tool shells; run every `just` recipe via
  `nix develop --impure --accept-flake-config -c …` from the workspace root, and
  nix itself needs the sandbox disabled (fetcher-cache SQLite write to
  `~/.cache/nix`).
- After `just deploy-production`, the production health flip is fast: Railway
  built + deployed ~3 minutes after CI went green on `production`
  (`curl https://obsign.org/xrpc/_health` → version).
- The manual docs pass (deploy.md "Release-time documentation pass") folds fine
  into the set-version PR; `just docs-screenshots` + `-check` both run clean on
  this Mac (where the PNG baselines are generated). See [[run-just-ci-pds-not-bare-clippy]].
- **`origin` has a DUAL push-url (GitHub + tangled knot), and `release.sh` /
  `deploy-production.sh` both `git push origin`** — which would push the tag /
  `production` branch to both remotes, so a tangled reject leaves an ambiguous
  half-push. Cleanest at release time (validated 2026-07-23, v0.7.2): skip the
  recipes and run their logic manually with **GitHub-only explicit pushes** —
  `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z"` then
  `git push git@mal.github.com:malpercio-dev/ezpds.git vX.Y.Z`, and advance
  production with `git push git@mal.github.com:...  <tag-commit>:refs/heads/production`
  (verify the FF first: current production must be an ancestor). This ALSO sidesteps
  the untracked-`devenv.lock` dirty-tree block, since the scripts' `git status`
  clean check is replaced by your own precheck. Verify each landed with
  `git ls-remote --tags origin` / a production fetch. See [[project_github_tangled_sync]].
- **Full ship sequence works via `gh` + the health endpoint, no Railway CLI:**
  merge PR (squash — repo convention, auto-deletes branch) → watch the workflow
  literally named **CI** on `main` (`gh run list --branch main`; the two
  `TestFlight` lanes are app distribution, NOT a PDS-deploy gate) → tag + advance
  production → watch **CI** on the `production` branch (runs the `verify-release`
  tag-match guard) → poll `https://obsign.org/xrpc/_health` for `version` to flip.
  The health host is NOT in the sandbox allowlist, so poll it with the sandbox
  disabled (a Monitor can't reach it; a `run_in_background` Bash loop can, and
  background `sleep` is allowed even though foreground `sleep` is blocked).

# Changelog

All notable user-visible changes to ezpds are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
Changes are collected in `changelog.d/` during development and inserted here when
`just set-version` prepares a release. There is intentionally no `Unreleased` section.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-08-08

### Added

- OAuth loopback client identifiers (`http://localhost?redirect_uri=…&scope=…`) are now supported, so a developer building an app against a locally running Custos can use the standard atproto development client instead of publishing a metadata document.

- Operators can now tune the OAuth access-token lifetime with `EZPDS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECS` (default 900 seconds, accepted range 1–1800). The conformance suite uses it to test what a client sees when its token expires.

- The OAuth conformance suite now covers confidential clients (`private_key_jwt`), and a client publishing its keys at a loopback `jwks_uri` is no longer refused for using plain http — the same development exception `client_id` resolution already made.

- The OAuth conformance suite now covers refresh-token rotation, including the concurrent-refresh case that used to log clients out silently.


### Changed

- User documentation is rewritten in plainer language for a security-minded audience, and the signing-in guide now documents push-to-approve with number matching.

- Obsign developer documentation moved from the app overview into module docs beside the code it describes; no runtime behavior changed.

- Server developer documentation moved from the crate overview into module docs beside the code it describes; no runtime behavior changed.

- Marketing site copy now speaks to the launch audience: security outcomes lead (ownership reads as the consequence, not the pitch), protocol vocabulary like rotation-key indexes and PLC moved off the Obsign page to the Custos and docs tiers, the recovery-share wording matches where shares actually live, and the privacy page accurately scopes what analytics records.

- The pages Custos renders in the browser now follow the writing-style guide's user register: OAuth error pages say what happened, what it means, and what to do next (with mechanical detail moved to the server log), the consent page's wallet path drops protocol vocabulary, and the landing page describes key custody in plain words.

- The wallet's everyday and onboarding copy now follows the writing-style guide's user register: protocol vocabulary ("rotation key", "PLC directory", "PDS", "tombstone", "did:web") is replaced with the established plain words ("deciding key", "the public record", "server", "retire", "domain identity") on every surface outside the advanced tier, and error messages state what happened and what to do next.

- The Brass Console drops the descriptive lede paragraph that opened every screen — the elements speak for themselves, with the load-bearing facts kept as one-liners (the accounts sort order and meter legend, the status screen's facts-not-verdict contract) — and the remaining prose loses its machine-flavored tells while keeping the operator register's protocol vocabulary untouched.

- Obsign's error surface now has a declared seam (ADR-0031): screens own every error sentence keyed on the typed `code`, diagnostic detail stays in the log (or a visibly subordinate detail slot), and server attribution is only ever true — a local Keychain failure can no longer render as "Your PDS reported: …". The recovery-override, identity-removal, and claim screens drop their raw error-chain interpolations for calm, styled sentences, and `get_available_user_domains` rejects with a typed error instead of a bare string. In the operator console, a relay's own rejection reason is now attributed to the relay and length-bounded instead of being spoken in the console's voice at whatever length the relay sent — so a server the operator doesn't run can't put words in their tools' mouth.

- A confidential OAuth client's published key set (`jwks_uri`) is now cached instead of fetched on every token request. Previously each token refresh added a round trip to the client's key host, and an outage there made the client unable to authenticate at all; the key is now reused for up to an hour (configurable via `[oauth] client_jwks_cache_ttl_secs`).


### Fixed

- Pushed authorization requests now record the client's DPoP key, and the token endpoint refuses a code bound to a different one. The binding currently reaches codes issued through the wallet consent path; the password consent form cannot carry it (its pushed request is already consumed by the time the form is submitted). The PAR endpoint also no longer requires a `state` parameter, and an authorization response no longer echoes an empty `state` back to a client that sent none.

- A device holding more than one identity on the same Custos instance now receives notifications for every one of them. Previously each identity's registration replaced the last one's route to the device, so only the most recently opened identity got pushes and the rest went silent with nothing to explain it.

- OAuth sessions now match the reference PDS's lifetimes and refresh semantics: access tokens live 15 minutes (was 5), refresh sessions 14 days (was 24 hours), and a concurrent duplicate refresh (multi-tab, background+foreground) no longer silently logs the client out — while replaying an old refresh token later revokes the whole session as a theft signal.

- The token endpoint now actually verifies `private_key_jwt` client authentication (RFC 7523, ES256, 30-second clock tolerance) instead of silently ignoring a confidential client's `client_assertion` and treating it as public. The client's registered `token_endpoint_auth_method` decides what is required, with keys taken from its metadata `jwks` or a policy-checked `jwks_uri` fetch.

- Granular `rpc:` OAuth scopes now match their `aud` on the service DID regardless of `#serviceId` fragments, so a grant written in either convention (bare DID or fragment-qualified) authorizes both PDS proxying and `getServiceAuth` consistently.

- XRPC endpoints now answer errors in the flat AT Protocol shape (`{"error": "ExpiredToken", "message": ...}`) with the canonical atproto error names, so third-party app sessions refresh instead of dying when an access token expires. The provisioning API's nested envelope is unchanged.

[Release v0.11.0 — PR #516](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/516) is open. Watching CI.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **`origin` here has a dual push-url** (GitHub + the tangled knot mirror), so a bare `git push origin` fans out to both — and a tangled rejection leaves an ambiguous half-push. That's why I pushed to the explicit GitHub URL instead. The same reasoning will apply to the tag and the `production` branch.
- **`set-version` restamped four generated pages automatically.** The operator reference docs carry a `Generated from source for ezpds vX.Y.Z` line, so *any* version bump makes them stale by definition and `docs-check` would fail the release PR on its first CI run. Folding the regeneration into `set-version` turns a recurring footgun into a non-event — the diff was exactly four stamp lines.
